title: Dative Case & Dative Triggers
subtitle: Spot Dative prepositions (mit, nach, aus, zu, von, bei) and Dative verbs (helfen, danken, gefallen) instantly.

cheatSheet.summary: The Dative case marks the indirect object (the recipient: 'to/for whom?') and is automatically triggered by a fixed set of Dative prepositions and Dative verbs.
keyTakeaways: Article shift: Masculine [M] der → dem, Neuter [N] das → dem, Feminine [F] die → der, Plural [PL] die → den (+n on the noun!).
Memory rule for Dative articles: 'M-R-M-N' (deM, deR, deM, deN).
Always-Dative prepositions: aus, bei, mit, nach, seit, von, zu, gegenüber.
Common contractions: zu + dem = zum, zu + der = zur, bei + dem = beim, von + dem = vom.

patterns.translation: He comes out of the house.

cheatSheet.watchOut: Don't panic when you see 'der' before a feminine noun! In the Dative, Feminine [F] 'die' transforms into 'der' ('mit der Frau', 'aus der Stadt').

exercises.prompt: Ich fahre jeden Morgen mit ___ Zug zur Arbeit.
exercises.english: I go to work by train every morning.
exercises.fullGerman: Ich fahre jeden Morgen mit dem Zug zur Arbeit.
exercises.rulePill: Preposition 'mit' ALWAYS triggers Dative → Masculine [M] 'der Zug' becomes 'dem Zug'.

exercises.prompt: Nach ___ Schule treffen wir uns im Café.
exercises.english: After school we meet at the café.
exercises.fullGerman: Nach der Schule treffen wir uns im Café.
exercises.rulePill: Preposition 'nach' triggers Dative → Feminine [F] 'die Schule' shifts to 'der Schule'.

exercises.prompt: Kannst du ___ Nachbarn beim Umzug helfen?
exercises.english: Can you help the neighbor with the move?
exercises.fullGerman: Kannst du dem Nachbarn beim Umzug helfen?

nouns.caseTrigger: Verb 'helfen' ALWAYS takes a Dative object

exercises.rulePill: 'helfen' is a pure Dative verb (Wem hilfst du?) → Masculine [M] 'der Nachbar' becomes 'dem Nachbarn'.

exercises.prompt: Die Lehrerin erklärt ___ Kindern die Grammatik.
exercises.english: The teacher explains the grammar to the children.
exercises.fullGerman: Die Lehrerin erklärt den Kindern die Grammatik.

nouns.caseTrigger: Indirect recipient of 'erklären' → Dative Plural adds '-n'

exercises.rulePill: In Dative Plural [PL], 'die' becomes 'den' AND the noun takes an extra '-n': 'den Kindern'.

exercises.promptHint: Find the wrong article after the Dative preposition 'aus'.
exercises.english: The dog runs out of the house.
exercises.fullGerman: Der Hund läuft aus dem Haus.
exercises.rulePill: Preposition 'aus' ALWAYS triggers Dative → Neuter [N] 'das Haus' changes to 'dem Haus'.

exercises.prompt: Wir wohnen seit ___ Jahr in Wien.
exercises.english: We have been living in Vienna for one year.
exercises.fullGerman: Wir wohnen seit einem Jahr in Wien.
exercises.rulePill: Preposition 'seit' triggers Dative → Neuter [N] 'ein Jahr' takes '-em': 'seit einem Jahr'.

exercises.promptHint: 'danken' is a classic Dative verb. Fix the pronoun!
exercises.english: I thank you for the help!
exercises.fullGerman: Ich danke dir für die Hilfe!
exercises.rulePill: 'danken' ALWAYS takes Dative (like helfen, gefallen, gehören) → use Dative 'dir', never Accusative 'dich'.

exercises.instruction: Order the sentence with Dative recipient BEFORE Accusative direct object.
exercises.english: I give my mother a bouquet of flowers.
exercises.fullGerman: Ich schenke meiner Mutter einen Blumenstrauß.
exercises.rulePill: When both objects are nouns, the Dative person ('meiner Mutter' [F]) comes BEFORE the Accusative thing ('einen Blumenstrauß' [M]).

exercises.prompt: Das neue Lied gefällt ___ sehr gut.
exercises.english: I really like the new song (literally: it pleases me).
exercises.fullGerman: Das neue Lied gefällt mir sehr gut.

nouns.caseTrigger: The song is the subject; the listener is in the Dative!

exercises.rulePill: With 'gefallen', the thing liked is the Nominative subject and the person who likes it takes Dative: 'mir'.
